svg.text: One terminal, three threads, many cursors
Blocking pty I/O stays on OS threads, so a slow reader backpressures the shell through the kernel's own buffer instead of growing a queue.
neither — a value or a channel
one copy of the bytes, one cursor per subscriber
hold back a torn UTF-8 tail, so
every flush end is a char boundary
the one copy of the bytes
a trim drops back to a flush
end, so head always lands on
two tokio tasks, and a cursor
hand each event to the attach
the other direction — plain RPC, no threads of its own
Replay and live output are the same bytes
A new attach starts at snapshot_floor, so its first
recv() is the retained scrollback and it streams on
from there. No second buffer to keep in step.
Lag is bounded in bytes, not in messages
A slow reader's slack is 256 KiB. Past that its cursor
falls below head and resumes there, seeing a gap —
A dropped client is not a dropped terminal
Closing a connection aborts run_stream and drops the
RingReader. The three threads and the ring are
untouched, which is what terminalAttach comes back to.
spawn_forward removes the terminal from the registry
when the child dies. terminalClose removes it and
